content.text: How can life insurance help with estate taxes?

Life insurance can provide immediate liquidity to pay estate taxes without forcing asset sales. When held in an ILIT (Irrevocable Life Insurance Trust), the death benefit is typically excluded from your taxable estate. Key considerations: your projected estate tax liability, premium affordability, and trust setup. What's your estimated estate size and do you currently have any life insurance?
What's the difference between term and whole life for estate planning?

Term provides coverage for a set period at lower premiums—useful if you expect estate tax liability to decrease. Whole life provides permanent coverage with cash value accumulation—better for permanent estate liquidity needs. For large estates, survivorship (second-to-die) policies are common since estate tax typically triggers at the second spouse's death. What are your goals: temporary coverage or permanent liquidity?
